page: Microsoft Azure E128s_v7 is an Esv7-family virtual machine configured with 128 dedicated vCPUs and 1024.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, and virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark results place the E128s_v7 in the top tier for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, PassMark CPU metrics, and static web serving throughput. It also achieves top-tier performance in Redis SET operations, processing 189.85 million operations per second. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and database operations are rated as strong. However, single-core stress-ng CPU performance and PassMark memory scores fall into the average category. For LLM inference, the server demonstrates top-tier prompt processing speeds for large 70B models, though text generation speeds for the same model size remain average.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1 and dedicated compute resources, the E128s_v7 offers high resource density for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. The lack of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, requiring external Premium Storage. The server is suited for large-scale database management, multi-threaded data processing, memory-cached key-value stores like Redis, static web serving at scale, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
